items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And then through The Stones I discovered Muddy Waters and Howlin’ Wolf and the roots.

ctx.x: What kind of songs would you have been playing?

Oh that was, you know, I mean “Strangers in the Night,” you know, “Spanish Eyes.” But standards. The Great American Songbook. Because this would have been like 1965. Round about there. So what I was listening to was not that at all. I was listening to The Beatles, The Stones, The Animals. And then through The Stones I discovered Muddy Waters and Howlin’ Wolf and the roots.
I love watching, playing with older fellas, you not only learn the music you watch how they operate with the audience, and taking requests and the whole thing about playing a gig.
